Seed.
SOMETHING ENTIRELY NEW AND UNIQUE.
An enthusiastic gardener has for several
years been
crossing and re-crossing all sorts of the Tomato, both large
and small, yellow, white and red, early and late. Every
known variety has been used—large, smooth, pear-shaped,
plum-shaped, currant, fig, peach, etc.
The result is a most
interesting mixture of all shapes, colors and sizes, from the
very largest to the very smallest.
This mixture is not only
novel but valuable, and the most interesting and satisfactory
to plant for the home garden.
Everybody will be delighted
with the variety and quality of fruit produced, and every-
body can find among them some particular kinds which suit
their individual taste better than others,

for 2c.
